items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business Administration, Accounting, Public Administration, or related field
Master’s degree (preferred)
Minimum 3 years of experience in research administration, grant admission, contract administration, financial management, budget development, or related business operations
Experience administering large federal, state, foundation, or cooperative agreement awards
Experience supporting pre-award and post-award sponsored research activities
Experience working with CA state agencies and government-funded programs
Demonstrated experience developing, monitoring, reconciling, and reporting on complex budgets
Experience developing grant proposals, funding submissions, and external partnerships with community organizations, foundations, and government agencies
Experience working within the University of California system, including knowledge of UC research administration policies and procedures
Experience using research and financial management systems such as UCPath, Oracle, Cayuse, ERS, or similar platforms

The Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior is seeking to hire a full-time Research Administrator to support the UCLA Tarjan Center and PEERs Clinic. We are a nationally recognized center dedicated to improving the lives of individuals with developmental and neurodevelopment disabilities. The Tarjan Center advances research, education, community engagement, and systems change initiatives that promote inclusion, independence, and quality of life across the lifespan.

You will provide comprehensive support for sponsored research administration and serve as key liaison among faculty, funding agencies, community organizations, and campus partners to ensure the successful administration and growth of federally, state, foundation, and privately funding programs. Key responsibilities:
Manage pre-award and post-award administration for sponsored research projects, grants, and contracts
Develop, monitor, reconcile, and analyze project budgets and financial reports
Coordinate grant proposal preparation, submission, and compliance activities
Administer contract, sub awards, and other sponsored project agreements
Support philanthropic partnerships, community collaborations, and strategic initiatives
Coordinate outreach, dissemination, conferences, trainings, and stakeholders engagement activities
Ensure compliance with sponsor, regulatory, and University requirements
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and financial reporting systems

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Knowledge of sponsored research administration principles federal grant regulations, and compliance requirements
Ability to interpret funding guidelines, contracts, and regulatory requirements
Strong project management skills with the ability to independently manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines
Excellent analytical, organizational, and written/verbal communication skills
